title: Medical and social assessment (disability)
what: A commission decides whether a person has a disability and what help they need. The decision is based on medical papers and an examination.
why: For lasting health problems after an illness or injury that make it hard to work or take care of yourself.
duration: gathering papers takes weeks, the assessment itself usually takes up to an hour, and the decision comes the same day or later
tell_doctor: All your illnesses and how they get in the way of life
Which medicines and treatment you get
Which aids you need: a cane, a wheelchair, a hearing aid
Difficulties with work, daily life, and getting around

prepare.title: Referral
prepare.text: Usually your treating doctor arranges the referral for assessment after the needed tests.

prepare.title: Papers
prepare.text: Collect discharge papers, reports, and test results. The more complete they are, the more accurate the decision.

prepare.title: Remote assessment
prepare.text: Sometimes the assessment is done without a visit, from papers. Check with your clinic.

bring: Work record or a note from work, if asked
steps: Your treating doctor sends you for tests
If an in-person exam is needed, you are invited
Specialists talk to you and examine you
The commission makes a decision and draws up a rehabilitation program
feel: The process can be long and tiring
after: You receive a certificate and a rehabilitation program
The decision can be appealed within the set time
Keep track of the date of re-assessment

faq.q: Can the assessment be done at home?
faq.a: If a person cannot come, a home visit or a papers-only assessment is possible. Check with your clinic.

faq.q: What if I disagree with the decision?
faq.a: It can be appealed. The office will explain the procedure and deadlines.

reminders.text: Medical and social assessment tomorrow. Check that all your papers and the referral are with you.
